title: Compare the type of a string and a number
description: Write a function `same_type(a, b)` that returns whether `a` and `b` have the same type, using `type()`.
hints: type(a) == type(b) compares the type objects themselves - '10' (a string) and 10 (an int) look similar when printed but are never the same type.
expected_behavior: Returns True if a and b have the same type.
solution:
def same_type(a, b):
    return type(a) == type(b)
explanation: A digit-looking string like '10' is never automatically treated as a number by Python - type() makes that distinction explicit rather than relying on == to also compare types (which it doesn't).
